svg.text: Every plane, what is committed and what is not, and the two query paths. Drawn from the code on 2026-09-12.
off by default, or not built
SOURCES -- WHAT COUNTS AS A DOCUMENT
INGEST -- THE ONLY PATH INTO THE COMMITTED PLANE
decode() returned nothing -> a row in .fux/enrich/queue.tsv with the reason. Queued, never silently dropped -- and the reason distinguishes "no decoder exists" from "a model is the only way".
THE COMMITTED PLANE -- THIS IS THE PRODUCT
256 shards, {00..ff}.jsonl, one canonical JSON line per document. Doc-major, sorted, so it diffs like code.
The shard is blake2b(doc id, 1 byte). A bundled git merge driver handles two branches touching the index.
field lengths; wlen is DERIVED at query time
display only -- the cap never touches ranking
of the RAW bytes -- what answer verifies against
git commit time. Recency never reads a clock.
kind + dst + grade: link, tag, supersedes, code
No content. Ever. The index holds statistics about your documents and never the documents -- that is L2, and it is why there is no second copy to go stale.
REQUIRED -- every verb but setup, tune,
output and doctor refuses without it
ORDERING only -- how results are sorted,
SHAPE only -- how a result is shown,
also committed: sources/ fetchers/ decoders/ enrich/ node/ fux refusals.toml formats.toml .fuxignore
THE TWO GITIGNORED PLANES -- AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF THING
fux build reconstructs all of it. Safe to delete, any time.
Carries CACHEDIR.TAG, so backup tools skip it unasked.
The bytes a fetch actually returned, for URLs whose line
says keep=true. Gitignored and tagged like derived --
Deleting it loses the only local copy. Getting it back means
re-fetching from a source that must still exist.
A third kind, not a subdivision of derived: runtime/ MEANS rebuildable.
.fux/.gitignore lists the ignored directories BY NAME and never a wildcard.
One .fux/* line would quietly drop the committed index from git with no error -- so fux doctor asserts this against git check-ignore itself.
QUERY -- EVERY CALL, AND THE LAW THAT LETS THERE BE TWO PATHS
Read every shard as raw bytes; parse a line only when it
substring-matches a query hash. No build step needed.
Accelerator -- only with --fast, only if fresh
Rarest-first, block-max bound, skip test. Falls through to
the scan silently when the stamp no longer matches.
Float addition is not associative, so the accelerator never
accumulates a score. It produces candidates and statistics;
rank() does every arithmetic operation, once, for both.
--fast can only ever change speed. That is asserted, not hoped.
expansion guard -> BM25F weight-then-saturate-once -> archived x superseded x recency x priority -> the declared 5-key sort -> ties marked before truncation
body 1.0 heading 3.0 title 2.0 path 1.5 ctx 1.0 k1 1.2 b 0.75 sort: (-round(score,9), superseded, -mtime, -priority, id)
Then: -q arms fused by RRF at k=60 - proximity rerank of the top 20 (OFF by default) - the confidence band - and for answer, the refer plane.
REFER -- THE ONLY PART THAT LEAVES THE MACHINE
fux answer ranks top-3, then goes and reads the source before it quotes.
file: reads the checkout - url: hits the TTL cache, else your fetcher under a hard timeout, else .fux/acquired/, else it says it did not look.
Then: chunk on headings (transient, never written) -> rescore with the same BM25F over the passage set -> assemble under 8000 bytes -> cite with a line range and a fresh sha.
THE TWO READERS -- ONE INDEX, ONE CONTRACT, AND A THIRD ARM OF THE LAW
Every verb, and the only thing that writes a committed byte.
Reference scan by default; the accelerator with --fast.
from fux import open -> ix.find / ask / answer
An importable read surface as of 2026-09-12, every result through the same output schema.
node -- fux-engine on npm, vendored to .fux/node/
ONE bundled fux.mjs + manifest, 244 KB, no build step FOR YOU. COMMITTED, because
the audience is a host with no Python to regenerate it with.
Rewritten at the head of every ingest when the engine version differs. Reads, never writes.
The differential law, third arm: python == node -- same ids, same order, same locators and band. The printed score is equal after round(9); the ORDER has no tolerance at all.

Three asymmetries are decisions, not gaps: Node never fetches, so url: is never current or cached - it rebuilds the graph plane in memory and needs no fux build - with no decoders, it declines what it cannot decode.
THE LAWS THIS SHAPE EXISTS TO SATISFY
dependencies = []. The zero-dependency guarantee was withdrawn 2026-09-06; a runtime dependency now needs an accepted record.
The index holds statistics. Chunks are re-derived transiently at answer time and written nowhere.
Same sources, byte-identical index. No wall clock, no filesystem order, no model.
ask and find never touch the network. Only ingest and answer can, and only through your fetcher.
Non-git sources commit hashed metadata, not values.
Not built, and named here so no one reads it off a diagram as shipped:
the paper's single content-addressed MST keyspace (L/ P/ D/ V/ E/ M/) -- what shipped is flat sharded JSONL. The dense / vector lane -- deleted 2026-08-25.
The ARC cache is implemented and tested but never constructed on the CLI path -- the cache that actually runs is the TTL fetch cache under .fux/runtime/.
